nom: NUDESTIX NUDESKIN Lemon-Aid Detox & Glow Micro-Peel

segments.oily: The reviewer with oily skin reports the peel left it hydrated without a greasy feel, and two more with combination-to-oily skin say it helps unclog pores and clear away impurities.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are split: a few find the peel drying or only mildly effective on dry patches, while more, including some with very dry or dry, acne-prone skin, say it leaves skin softer without stripping or drying it further.
segments.combination: The reviewers who describe their skin as combination-to-oily say the peel unclogs pores and removes impurities without irritating their skin.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including one who calls her skin severely sensitive, overwhelmingly report no redness, burning, or irritation, though a couple note the exfoliating action can still feel like a bit much and suggest patch-testing first.
segments.mature: Reviewers who mention their age or fine lines, including a 47-year-old with hyperpigmentation and a 61-year-old, report brighter, softer skin and, in one case, visibly smoother texture despite the peel's unusual feel.

concerns.aging: The one reviewer who names fine lines as her main concern says this was the first peel or scrub that actually worked for her, leaving her texture visibly smoother and her pores minimized; a 61-year-old reviewer separately reports her skin looking great with regular use.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers who focus on hydration say the peel left dry patches and winter dryness noticeably softer without stripping the skin further, and one with oily skin even calls it hydrating; a minority instead found it left skin feeling dry afterward, with one calling it 'a bit drying' for the price.
concerns.redness: The large majority of reviewers, including several with self-described sensitive skin, report no redness or irritation at all; one exception describes the peel making her skin a bit red, though she calls it nothing serious.
concerns.barrier: Most reviewers who comment on their skin barrier say the peel does not strip or leave skin feeling tight the way other peels do; one reviewer, by contrast, says she specifically likes the light tightening sensation it leaves behind.
concerns.spots: Reviewers dealing with hyperpigmentation, discoloration, or acne marks say the peel helped brighten and even out their skin and reduce the visible marks over time, describing it as suited for dullness and pigmentation issues, though the effect is gradual rather than dramatic.
concerns.blemishes: Most acne-prone reviewers report the peel calmed breakouts or worked well through an active acneic phase without irritation, but there is dissent: one reviewer had terrible breakouts after using it, and another saw new blemishes appear that she attributed to purging.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily or combination skin say the peel unclogs pores, reduces sebum and blackheads around the nose, and leaves a matte finish without over-drying or feeling greasy.

aspects.libelle: Messy, best used over a sink

extraits.texte: This has a strong scent and I had terrible breakouts after using it. The texture is very strange and balls up on the skin. Would not recommend.

I patch tested this product before using as I have dry skin and sometimes peels can give me a reaction. While I had no reaction I did fi nd it a bit drying. The product smells nice but for the price IMO it is not worth it.

extraits.titre: When Life Gives You Lemons: A Review of Nudestix Lemon Aid
extraits.texte: The Nudestix Lemon Aid Detox and Glow Micro Peel is a facial product that promises to detoxify and brighten your skin. With an attractive packaging and refreshing citrus scent it certainly starts off on the right foot. Yet the texture can be a bit surprising - it's less of a peel or mask and more akin to a damp facial wash reminiscent of water-soaked toilet paper.As a 47-year-old woman with hyperpigmentation and slightly dry skin I found that this product did provide some benefits despite its unconventional texture.Pros:Scent: The aroma of freshly squeezed lemons is invigorating and delightful. It offers a sensory experience that is refreshing.Packaging: The product comes in aesthetically pleasing packaging adding a touch of luxury to your skincare routine.Effectiveness: Despite its textural shortcomings it does leave your skin feeling softer and looking brighter. It seems to help with hyperpigmentation and dry skin to some extent.Cons:Texture: The biggest drawback is the product's texture. It feels like spreading wet toilet paper on your face which is not exactly the spa-like treatment one might hope for.Misleading Name: The name suggests a peel or mask but the consistency and application are more in line with a facial wash.Best Uses:This product can be a good addition to your skincare routine if you prioritize scent and brightness over texture. It's particularly suited for those with slight hyperpigmentation and dry skin as it does seem to offer some improvement in these ar

To be honest I was a little hesitant to try the mask. I have severely sensitive skin and most products make me itch or feel like it's burning my face. I finally tried it and was pleasantly surprised! This product was so gentle on my skin and I had absolutely no reaction to it. I will definitely be purchasing this product in the future! There was only one downer about this mask. It's messy with your massaging it on your skin. So make sure you do it over the sink

I have dry acne prone skin which is susceptible to hyperpigmentation from acne marks so I was excited to try this product. It did not disappoint ! My skin feels brighter and smoother after using this product and helps prevent breakouts. It's not too harsh and doesn't irritate my skin - just make sure you don't use at the same time as any actives to avoid irritation. As an example I will not use retin- A directly after using this peel. It doesn't dry out my skin even though I have very dry skin
